relationships.subject: IL-1β
relationships.evidence_quote: Upregulation of CaV2.2 is driven by increased expression of interleukin-1beta (IL-1β) in uninjured DRG neurons.

relationships.subject: Cdk5
relationships.evidence_quote: It has been shown that recombinant CaV3.2 channels expressed in HEK 293 cells are phosphorylated by cyclin-dependent kinase 5 (Cdk5) at Ser561 and Ser1987 [9].

relationships.subject: Egr-1
relationships.evidence_quote: Early growth response 1 (Egr-1) enhances CaV3.2 expression, while repressor element 1-silencing transcription factor (REST) suppresses it [61].

relationships.subject: HMGB1
relationships.evidence_quote: Intraperitoneal administration of an anti-HMGB1-neutralizing antibody and a RAGE antagonist prevented the upregulation of both Egr-1 and thus CaV3.2 in L4 DRG neurons.

relationships.subject: USP5
relationships.evidence_quote: Through its deubiquitinating function, USP5 is believed to protect CaV3.2 channels from proteosomal degradation and is associated with the development of inflammatory and neuropathic pain [60,63].

key_findings: Review: ion channels (CaV2.2, CaV3.2, NaV1.3) are dysregulated in spared/uninjured DRG neurons after nerve injury and associate with neuropathic pain.
CaV3.2 upregulation in spared neurons is regulated by Cdk5 phosphorylation, HMGB1/RAGE-Egr-1 transcription and USP5 deubiquitination.
